title: The Blinding of Polyphemus
hypothesis: The Blinding reads as men against a giant, not men inside one, if the blocking keeps every body clear of the sleeping giant's arms, of the pen and its fence, and of each other, and the stake is carried in from the floor beside him; and the take gets a camera plan (the published cut predates the cinematographer and two of its frames were inside the giant).
variable: Blocking only (odyssey/keyframes/OD-B09-S09.json): K1 Odysseus from inside the pen under the giant's left hand to the floor beside it (121,-23), the bearers off the pen's fence and its corner; K2 the men round the stake's far end clear of the giant's thighs and the rocks; K3 the stake aimed into the eye from his left over the shoulder (dir -0.6, 0.32, -0.73), Odysseus and three bearers on the floor along it, spaced 55-75 units for their crested helmets, the perch on his chest removed; K4 the scatter east and west of his rise, no paths crossing. The marks re-read from the take, the score re-authored and compiled from the same direction module (the needles' events identical: asleep 25.4, glow 33.0, decide 39.0, thrust 43.4, roar 50.4), the camera plan made by tools/cinematographer/plan.js (31 shots).

result: Published as take 2. Odysseus waits beside the giant's hand, the stake goes into the eye from his left with the men on the floor. Loose: the thrust is mostly filmed from above the giant's head (a close of the crown with the blood, then down the stake), so the four men are small in it; two wides in the scatter (about 52-55 s) hold mostly the dark set with the risen giant behind the rocks; the stake now passes over the giant's shoulder rather than up from his chest as on the Eleusis amphora.
